builder_plan.scenario: Your inference service slows down when several customers send requests together.
builder_plan.change: Replay a recorded request trace with only the proposed serving policy changed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current scheduler on the same model and hardware.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Requests meeting your latency target, throughput, failures, and cost per successful request.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Introducing Cluster Efficiency to LLM Serving: Pooling Economical Accelerators over Fast Interconnects
summary: The method replaces an eight-GPU RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell server for long-context LLM serving with a Tenstorrent Galaxy cluster of pooled economical accelerators connected by fast interconnects. It requires specialized hardware with integrated communication engines, pipelined ring transfers, communication-computation overlap, and device-side decode replay, which imposes a high engineering and acquisition cost. The approach can fail if the interconnect is not sufficiently fast, as TCP-class communication reduces throughput by 23.5-67.4% and eliminates the cost advantage.
rationale: This technique is not applicable to the reader's constrained infrastructure, as it requires a specialized Tenstorrent Galaxy cluster rather than a single 24 GB GPU or third-party APIs.
technique: Pooling economical accelerators over fast interconnects

claims.statement: The method replaces an eight-GPU RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell server for long-context LLM serving with a Tenstorrent Galaxy cluster of pooled economical accelerators connected by fast interconnects. It requires specialized hardware with integrated communication engines, pipelined ring transfers, communication-computation overlap, and device-side decode replay, which imposes a high engineering and acquisition cost. The approach can fail if the interconnect is not sufficiently fast, as TCP-class communication reduces throughput by 23.5-67.4% and eliminates the cost advantage.

Across three dense models in BF16 and 8-bit configurations with 8K-256K-token contexts, the Galaxy achieves 1.07-2.24x the tokens per dollar of an eight-GPU RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell server under a three-year acquisition-and-electricity cost model. Emulating TCP-class communication on the same chips reduces throughput by 23.5-67.4% and eliminates the cost advantage in every evaluated configuration.
